page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical execution core using two threads per core. The server provides 16.0 GB of system memory, which represents an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, reflecting an elevated 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio characteristic of memory-optimized families.

The r8ib.large includes no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage solutions for persistent data retention. It contains no integrated graphics processing units or hardware accelerators. Networking is configured with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and instances are deployed without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Users must account for network throughput limits when sizing external volume attachment for I/O-heavy operations.

By offering substantial memory capacity relative to its 2 vCPUs, the r8ib.large allows memory-heavy tasks to operate efficiently without overprovisioning unneeded compute cores. This configuration delivers solid resource efficiency for workloads where memory footprint dictates instance sizing. Primary operational fits include in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, small-to-medium relational databases, and data transformation microservices requiring moderate compute paired with ample memory.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz, the instance exposes 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, specifically suited for memory-bound applications. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and features no local instance storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely on networked storage volumes. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU allocation minimizes the need to scale compute resources simply to satisfy memory footprint demands. The r8ib.large instance fits in-memory caching systems, lightweight relational or key-value databases, and memory-intensive microservices.
